(1) N-GLARE: latent-only, over 40 models, under 1 percent of the token and runtime cost, output-free, peer-reviewed [3][4]. Two independent papers report that prompt-side HARM-RECOGNITION geometry is essentially INVARIANT to abliteration: abliterated variants match their instruction-tuned counterparts within 0.003 AUROC across 12 models spanning four families [5], and at most 0.015 AUROC on Qwen base/instruct/abliterated triplets [10]. Put this in every lane's power calculation.\n\nTHE SECOND MOST CONSEQUENTIAL, ALSO NEW. A parent-free, single-checkpoint, interaction-flavoured activation scalar already exists and already failed. HRCI_repr is defined as one half the absolute inner product of the harmfulness and refusal carrier directions plus one half the mean squared canonical correlation between their local subspaces, with the equal weighting fixed a priori rather than optimised against outcomes [12]. Put this in every lane's power calculation.\n\nTHE SECOND MOST CONSEQUENTIAL, ALSO NEW. A parent-free, single-checkpoint, interaction-flavoured activation scalar already exists and already failed. HRCI_repr is defined as one half the absolute inner product of the harmfulness and refusal carrier directions plus one half the mean squared canonical correlation between their local subspaces, with the equal weighting fixed a priori rather than optimised against outcomes [12]. It is tracked over 100 checkpoints per regime against XSTest refusal, attack success rate, StrongREJECT and benign utility, falling from 0.0784 at step 50 to 0.0205 at step 500 while fixed-source ASR rises from 0 to 0.2500 and XSTest refusal falls from 1.0000 to 0.2280, with an SFT control moving only from 0.0217 to 0.0190 while staying high-ASR [12]. The authors' own verdict is that low coupling is not a safety score, and that the dense all-anchor results support a fixed-protocol diagnostic rather than a general safety score [12]. That is the closest published object to this run's own ambition, and it is a scaled negative result. It is now mandatory baseline G10, it is implementable in a few lines, and the paper must answer it rather than cite it in passing.\n\nA THIRD ADVERSE PRIOR LANE A MUST PRICE IN. Activation probes evaluated on XSTest-style matched twin cohorts - exactly lane A's item type - reach only AUROC 0.590 to 0.690 on the full Twin-n163 cohort and 0.656 to 0.819 on the guard-selected Twin-n70 subset under fixed transfer without pair-boundary fitting, and the paper concludes these scores behave as broad-risk detectors rather than standalone context adjudicators [11]. If lane A's twin numbers land above that band, check for leakage before celebrating. The behavioural counterpart is that risk genuinely does change between prompt and response - 61 percent of responses reduce harm relative to the prompt, 36 percent preserve it and 3 percent escalate - but that analysis is human-labelled and behavioural, not activation-level, so it is a weaker relative to K1 than the recon feared [30].\n\nBASELINE SPECS (full text in research_report.md section 7). G1 card/repo regex in BOTH term-swept and name-free variants, reported separately or the baseline is inflated by the very label it predicts. G2 black-box greedy refusal rate with the named safe-completion-opener failure mode. G3 first-token refusal logit gap, logit-only and therefore a baseline under the run invariant. G4 Fisher-ratio activation cluster separation over the upper-middle layer band, calibrated against the realistic published effect size of Pearson r equal to minus 0.546 between an activation sigma and behavioural compliance over 14 configurations [17]. G5 held-out difference-in-means with the mandatory high-dimension in-sample AUROC-1.000 warning, copying the published protocol of 100 labelled examples per class under a strict three-way split and reporting TPR at 1 percent FPR alongside AUROC, because that paper's central methodological point is that TPR varies by more than ten times the AUROC gap [6]. G6 raw hidden vectors as the non-featurised control. G7 JSS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE [3]. G8 GFS [7], the two-signal z-sum [13] and CANARY [24] are all PARENT-REQUIRING and must sit in a separate column. Analysis\n\nRefusal directions are extracted using the difference-in-means method, which computes mean activation differences between harmful and harmless prompt contexts at specific layers and token positions. When applying logit lens to refusal directions, the method can validate that identified refusal directions genuinely capture a model's safety mechanisms, with results showing that the refusal direction corresponds to refusal words when projected back to vocabulary space.\n\n## Unembedding and Readout\n\nA lens reading reflects both the hidden state and the readout (the unembedding matrix) used to decode it. The Sparse Readout Prism (SRP) method decomposes the readout using only its weights and expresses any token logit or logit difference as a sum of contributions from sparse readout features.\n\n## Safety Applications\n\nSafety audits can use SRP to define group contrasts for refusal and track feature contributions across paraphrases, languages, and adversarial prompts, treating recurring features as nominations for causal tests.\n\nThe search results show active research applying these mechanistic interpretability techniques to understand and audit AI safety mechanisms in language models."], "durationSeconds": 7.143543896999996, "searchCount": 1}

Planned the iteration-2 RESEARCH artifact for run_YqmEFECOIR3D (Qwen3-4B safety metric, recognition-vs-execution headline) on 2026-09-21. Findings from live search that the artifact direction did not know:

**THE BIG ONE — the headline axis is already half-published, and NOT by either paper the direction names.** arXiv:2606.24952, Galeone, Ettorre, Park, Ettorre, Ligorio, *"Perfect Detection, Failed Control: The Geometry of Knowing vs. Steering in Language Models"* (23 Jun 2026) publishes a **weight-computable** cosine between a detection direction and a control direction: AUC 1.000 from layer 5, cos = 0.12 (~83°), cos in [0.12, 0.20] across 4 models / 3 families / 1B–9B, **identical before and after instruction tuning (0.1197 vs 0.1200)**, and closes with "the cosine is a weight-computable signature of the dissociation between knowing and steering, **not a predictor of it**." That is candidate X6 (the R−E gap as a deployable scalar) one concept over — hallucination and output format, not harm — with an *adverse* conclusion attached. The direction listed six candidates and omitted X6; the plan adds it as a mandatory seventh. Remaining margin is only: harm concept, abliterated checkpoint (2606.24952 evaluates none), and a rate that varies across checkpoints.

**Live-verified seed IDs per lane** (planner searches, 2026-09-21):
- X1 accumulator gain → 2605.20241 Geometry-Lite (layer-wise margin geometry; iter1 called it the closest cousin to any layer-profile summary), 2602.04931, 2608.08904
- X2 write mass → 2607.01854 (its **weight-recovery energy** may BE X2; deciding question is parent-free vs reference-anchored), 2605.16600 "Where Pretraining writes and Alignment reads", 2601.08489, 2512.13655, 2608.05578 AMS
- X3 analytic percept-to-refusal gain → **2609.01936 Sparse Readout Prism** decomposes the readout *using only its weights* into per-token logit contributions and mentions refusal safety audits — likeliest closer; also 2605.28553
- X5 routing concentration → 2609.04721, 2609.14759, 2605.00236, plus HARC 2607.00572 itself
- X8 execution depth lag → 2604.22128 "Dissociating Decodability and Causal Use", **2608.17843 "Encoded but Not Actionable: the Decode-Generate-Steer Gap"**
- X10 weights-only scar → 2607.01854 failure map, ORBA HF blog (grimjim), and the named tool **Jorak Model Scanner** (from the sibling fcYd run) which may ship it already
- Dose curves (direction item 5) → 2512.13655 (minimum effective dose = smallest weight value giving ≥30% judged bypass; MMLU max degradation 0.028), 2607.17427 "Abliteration Is Not a Scalpel"

**Verified live, correcting the draft:** 2603.27412 = "The Geometry of Harmful Intent: Training-Free Anomaly Detection via Angular Deviation in LLM Residual Streams", Isaac Llorente-Saguer, 28 Mar 2026 — the *direction's* stated title is right, the *draft's* is invented. 2604.18901 = "Harmful Intent as a Geometrically Recoverable Feature of LLM Residual Streams", same sole author, 20 Apr 2026; abstract prints AUROC 0.982 / TPR@1%FPR 0.797, and the low-FPR argument verbatim ("TPR@1%FPR varies by more than ten times the AUROC gap").

**iter1 research_out.json schema** (reuse it): `title, layman_summary, summary, answer, sources, follow_up_questions`; each source = `index, url, title, summary, authors, year, supporting_passages[{quote, locator}]`. Companion `research_verification.json` carries `passage_check_scope` + per-passage `source_url/status/match_type/context`. Regex-recovered numbers from beyond the ~50KB fetch truncation are logged as **anchor/provenance entries, never as quoted passages** — keep the two classes separate.
